A peer to peer site is what you're talking about. That's not how voat is setup but it wouldn't be a bad idea. Maybe something like a peer to peer mirror or something. The problem come in when you try to scale something like voat. It becomes too much load for each peer to keep syncing all the content and comments.

There are solutions to the scaling. In particular not each peer needs to have everything. The obvious question is what if somebody wants something and all the peers that have it are unavailable? Imagine we have 1000 active users and we split the content 50/50. 500 active peers makes the chances of any given piece of content being unavailable basically 0. Add in dynamic peer balancing where if group 1 starts to get smaller than group 2 then some of group 2 automatically becomes group 1 members and I think we can change basically 0 to literally zero. And this scales up infinitely. If you have 2000 users then there are groups with 1/4 of the content each, and so on. If this was intelligently implemented it would dwarf client-server in every single way, and it's far from impossible. Making it completely secure is a lot more difficult, but there are also an enormous number of possibilities there.

I was considering working on this as my next project, but back when I was looking into this (maybe a year or two ago) there were a ton of peer-to-peer web type projects already well along in development.

what if the sub was encrypted. Controlled by central voat?

The cost of being a mod is hosting an enctryped remote server. You wouldnt be able to inject anything into it, but it processes the content as assigned by voat.

Yes, if you only had one mod, them going offline would also take down the sub, but if you had 3 mods on a sub, it could point to whoever has the least current bandwidth

There might be a solution here but it's not immediately obvious to me. Just calling it an encrypted server seems kind of hand wavey unless you have a more specific idea. The problem is:

  • A goes to site B
  • B sends a request to site C
  • C delivers to the content directly to A
  • B somehow needs to verify that the content being delivered to A is authentic before C delivers it

The big issue is that B can't trust a hash, but also cannot be the one delivering the content so he kind of has to.

What if C delivers content directly to A, but the moderator cluster application of C has a cross check application to validate the data without B? Similar to the BTC solving application where everyones application plays a part in the validation process before distributing the btc.

Then you have C guaranteeing that what C's sending is safe which is not a spot where you want to be.

BTC is just a validation by majority. Here it's a bit different since we have one trusted individual, B, trying to validate all the data being sent without actually accessing it. It's pretty tough!
